newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Faulding aims to gain pharmacy market share.
newsitem.headline: Faulding aims to gain pharmacy market share.

text.p: Pharmaceutical manufacturer F.H. Faulding and Co Ltd said on Wednesday it expected its new retail pharmacy strategy to immediately lift profits and to significantly increase its market share over five years.

Healthcare division chief operating officer David Murphy told Reuters Faulding hoped to lift its estimated 38.1 percent share of Australia's A$3.4 billion wholesale pharmaceutical market to at least 40 percent over the next five years.
"With the sorts of turnover we are talking in this industry, that is pretty significant," he said from Sydney.

Faulding earlier announced its healthcare division would offer Australia's 5,000 pharmacies a choice of four national retail brands targeted at distinct market segments, in a move to stave off competition from other retail sectors including supermarkets and brand stores such as The Body Shop.
Murphy said the brand strategy would underpin the current gross margins of Faulding's business by improved operating efficiencies and increased turnover.
While he would not disclose any earnings targets for the strategy, he said it would have an immediate impact on profits.
"Suffice to say we are looking upon our wholesale business from classically being the cash cow of the organisation to one that we see strong profit growth in," he said.

Murphy said the object of the strategy was to entice consumers to pharmacies as shopping destinations "as distinct from just the place to get your script filled" and to shake out many of the operating inefficiencies in the supply chain.

The gap between over-the-counter retail sales and prescription sales had continued to widen with prescriptions now accounting for 62.5 percent of total pharmacy turnover, compared to 50 percent in 1990, he said.

"If we are able to stop the rot and increase the size of the retail turnover in pharmacies, obviously Faulding, with such a strong market share, is going to be a beneficiary right along the supply line," he said, adding the company was blocked by competition rules from acquisition based growth.
"Our wholesale business is a major part of what we do and it has got to be protected and embellished and this is what this is all about," he said.

Murphy said pharmacies which allied themselves to the brands - Life, healthsense, The Medicine Shoppe, and Chem mart - would have access to significant savings from fittings through to payroll and inventory control.
"There is a lot of inefficiency in the (supply) chain right now and we intend to improve that," he said.

Murphy said Faulding had no ambition to own retail pharmacies and was lobbying the government against any radical changes to the current system but would quickly consider ownership if the market was opened to incorporated enterprises.
"We would prefer not to be involved ... (but) if a corporation was able to own a chain of pharmacies, Faulding would activate its options one nano-second later," he said.
